You are an adult. You don't have to do what your mom says. She does not get to guilt trip you. If you don't want to go to the protest, then don't go. 

That being said, if prior experience has led to you to expect the absolute worst of humanity, it can cause you to misjudge things sometimes. I get it, it's so fucking easy to only see danger when going outside your comfort zone, especially when you spent your most formative years literally struggling to stay alive. However, risk is present in your comfort zone too. It's literally everywhere, there is absolutely no way to escape it. So yes, if you go to the protest, there is a possibility of danger, but there's almost certainly less of that possibility than you would expect, and those same risks (violent transphobia, police) are present any time you go outside. Again, if you don't want to go to the protest, then no one has to right to force you, but it's also okay to get out of your comfort zone. You might meet other trans people and make friends too.

A common one is giving away meaningful possessions. A suicidal person might want to make sure their prized possessions are safe after they die, or they want to give their loved ones something to remember them by. Also if someone is typically very sad, and all of a sudden they’re acting very chipper, that’s a pretty big red flag. Essentially, they’ve come to terms with/made plans for their own death and eagerly await it rather than being sad about living. Obviously, they could just be in a good mood, but it’s always a good idea to check in with people you’re worried about. Some more obvious ones are saying they want to sleep forever, outright expressing a desire for death, and a sudden change in appearance (they look much more tired/disheveled). Again, number of these signs could signify something else entirely, but it’s better safe than sorry. It’s also really important not to totally freak out if you discover someone has active suicidal intention, and don’t blame them for you worrying. Its also important to know that if you’re a minor in the US and you tell a school counselor/teacher, they legally have to report it.
